title: Honey never really goes off
content: Archaeologists have found pots of honey in ancient Egyptian tombs that were still edible. Low water and high acidity stop bacteria growing.

title: Octopuses have three hearts
content: Two hearts pump blood through the gills and one through the body. Their blood is blue because it carries copper, not iron.

title: Bananas are berries. Strawberries aren't.
content: In botany a berry grows from one flower with one ovary. Bananas qualify; strawberries carry their seeds on the outside and don't.

title: A day on Venus is longer than its year
content: Venus takes about 243 Earth days to spin once, but only about 225 to orbit the Sun. It also spins backwards.

title: Oxford is older than the Aztec Empire
content: Teaching at Oxford had begun by 1096. Tenochtitlan, the Aztec capital, was founded in 1325.

title: Cleopatra lived closer to the Moon landing than to the Great Pyramid
content: The Great Pyramid was built around 2560 BC. Cleopatra died in 30 BC, about 2,000 years before Apollo 11.

title: Sharks are older than trees
content: Sharks have been around for roughly 450 million years. The first true trees appeared about 385 million years ago.

title: Wombats make cube-shaped poo
content: The cubes form in the last part of the intestine and stop the droppings rolling away from the rocks and logs wombats use as markers.

title: The Eiffel Tower grows in summer
content: Iron expands in heat, so the tower can be up to about 15 cm taller on a hot day.

title: There are more possible chess games than atoms in the universe
content: Claude Shannon estimated about 10^120 possible games. The observable universe has roughly 10^80 atoms.

title: Scotland's national animal is the unicorn
content: The unicorn has been a Scottish heraldic symbol since the 12th century and appears on the royal coat of arms.

title: The shortest war lasted under an hour
content: The Anglo-Zanzibar War of 27 August 1896 lasted between 38 and 45 minutes.

title: A teaspoon of neutron star weighs about a billion tonnes
content: Neutron stars pack more mass than the Sun into a ball about 20 km across.

title: Butterflies taste with their feet
content: Taste receptors on their feet tell them whether a leaf is the right place to lay eggs.

title: You can't see the Great Wall from the Moon
content: It is long but only a few metres wide. Astronauts say it is hard to spot even from low Earth orbit.

title: Lightning strikes Earth about 44 times a second
content: That is roughly 1.4 billion flashes a year, mostly over land near the tropics.

title: Sloths can hold their breath for 40 minutes
content: By slowing their heart rate, sloths can stay underwater far longer than dolphins.

title: The Pringles can inventor was buried in one
content: Fredric Baur designed the can. When he died in 2008, some of his ashes were buried in a Pringles tube.

title: Water expands about 9% when it freezes
content: That is why ice floats and why frozen pipes burst.

title: Sunlight is eight minutes old
content: Light takes about 8 minutes 20 seconds to travel from the Sun to Earth.

title: Everest isn't the farthest point from Earth's centre
content: Earth bulges at the equator, so the summit of Chimborazo in Ecuador is about 2 km farther from the centre.

title: Nintendo began in 1889 selling playing cards
content: Fusajiro Yamauchi founded it in Kyoto to make hanafuda cards, almost a century before Mario.

title: Ketchup was once sold as medicine
content: In the 1830s, tomato ketchup was marketed in the US as a cure for indigestion.

title: A blue whale's heart weighs about 180 kg
content: It is the largest heart of any animal, and its beat can be detected from kilometres away.

title: Tardigrades have survived open space
content: In 2007 these half-millimetre animals were exposed to vacuum and radiation outside a spacecraft, and some survived.

title: Astronauts get taller in space
content: Without gravity the spine stretches, and astronauts can grow up to about 3% taller until they return.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Effect of spaceflight on the human body

title: 'Robot' comes from the Czech for forced labour
content: Karel Čapek's 1920 play R.U.R. introduced the word, from 'robota'.

title: Australia is wider than the Moon
content: The Moon is about 3,474 km across. Australia measures about 4,000 km from east to west.

title: Russia spans 11 time zones
content: When it's breakfast in Kaliningrad, it's late evening in Kamchatka.

title: The first computer bug was a real moth
content: In 1947 engineers found a moth stuck in the Harvard Mark II and taped it into the logbook as the 'first actual case of bug being found'.

title: Flamingos are pink because of their food
content: Carotenoid pigments in the algae and shrimp they eat turn their feathers pink.

title: A group of flamingos is a flamboyance
content: It's a real collective noun, alongside a murder of crows and a parliament of owls.

title: Antarctica is the world's largest desert
content: A desert is defined by low rainfall, not heat. Antarctica gets very little precipitation.

title: Saturn would float in water
content: Its average density is about 0.69 g/cm³, lower than water's 1 g/cm³. You'd just need a big enough bath.

title: The dot over an i is called a tittle
content: The word dates back centuries and also covers the dot over a j.

title: Humans glow in the dark, very faintly
content: A 2009 study in Japan found the body emits visible light about 1,000 times too weak for our eyes to see.

title: Koalas sleep up to 20 hours a day
content: Eucalyptus is low in energy, so koalas save it by sleeping most of the day.

title: Ocean plankton make about half our oxygen
content: Phytoplankton photosynthesise like plants and produce roughly half of Earth's oxygen.

title: The Hundred Years' War lasted 116 years
content: It ran from 1337 to 1453, with long truces in between.

title: Your stomach gets a new lining every few days
content: Stomach lining cells are replaced quickly so the acid doesn't digest the stomach itself.
